Overview & History

* Founded: July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHrOzAVRPAfno8XVUSYTCscLx6WoKIQYvdajKWm_kyfhpPvvg0FYQ73zWRVddc_Vt4r4C0f919rDnJDKLJ9oFtMkvFF2il_K2BwjOheAGwSHFjgcldoCKZf0ply3L8G8MzECuU-RYN9mWOrK950)]

[[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHrOzAVRPAfno8XVUSYTCscLx6WoKIQYvdajKWm_kyfhpPvvg0FYQ73zWRVddc_Vt4r4C0f919rDnJDKLJ9oFtMkvFF2il_K2BwjOheAGwSHFjgcldoCKZf0ply3L8G8MzECuU-RYN9mWOrK950)]

* Author Libraries: Curated collections of contemporary poet pages containing biographies, photos, essays, and links to online works. findings: THE DATE OF THE ARTICLE. 'Founded: July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein.' This is the saved Wikipedia article ('It was founded on July 10, 1994 by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein'); the center's own About page gives another year: 'EPC was founed by Loss Peqeño Glazier, with Charles Bernstein, at the Poetics Program of SUNY-Buffalo in 1995.' The census row keeps both; the composition carries one. E-Poetry 2001 is the article's ('the sponsor of E-Poetry 2001, the world's first festival exclusively dedicated to electronic poetry').

THE CENTER LEFT AT BUFFALO. 'Origin: Created as part of the Poetics Program at the State University of New York (SUNY) at Buffalo.' The About page: 'In 2003, EPC began its active collaboration with the Center for Programs in Contemporary Writing (CPCW) at the University of Pennsylvania, including its sister site, PennSound.' and names 'Al Filreis , Publisher'; the home page tells readers to 'substitute "writing.upenn.edu/epc/" for "epc.buffalo.edu/"'. The composition's first card is the center at the University of Pennsylvania, and its body never names Penn; the ELMCIP card still gives 'glazier@buffalo.edu'. The article the composition follows was 'last edited on 2 March 2024'.

THE FIELD'S OWN RECORD NOT CARRIED. The About page: 'We also house the archives of the Buffalo Poetics Program from its fouding in 1991 to 2003 and of the Poetics List (1993-2014), the first poetry listserv discussion group.' The census row reads the EPC as holding a field's authors beside the field's discussion of itself; the composition carries the authors ('Curated collections of contemporary poet pages containing biographies, photos, essays, and links to online works') and the E-Poetry section, and leaves out the Poetics List and the Program archive. The goal on the About page ('resources centered on digital and contemporary formally innovative poetries, new media writing, and literary programming') is not stated.
